clue.text: Flag officer?

definitions.meaning: a flag flown by a ship to show its nationality
the most junior commissioned rank in the US Navy, and once in the British army

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a national banner at a ship's stern and a lowly commissioned rank.

clue.text: Eleven, being free, take in work and make a packet

indicators.note: the rearranged letters surround the abbreviation for work, enclosing it
letters set free are released from their order, so the word eleven is rearranged

parts.note: the word eleven supplies the letters to be rearranged
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Eleven people, having been freed, take on some work and earn a lot of money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make a packet' looks like the British idiom for earning lots of money, but 'packet' is the definition. OP is the usual short form of opus, a musical work.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: a paper wrapper or sleeve for letters or documents.

clue.text: Put up with the closed shop

definitions.text: Put up with the closed shop

parts.words: Put up with the closed shop
parts.note: reads as tolerating a union-only workplace, but means panels raised over windows when a shop is closed

explanation.walkthrough: A 'closed shop' is a workplace where all staff must join the union; here it is just a shop that has shut for the day.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: hinged or roller panels fitted over shop windows when trading stops.

clue.text: Entrance for spectators

definitions.meaning: an opening in a fence or wall
the number of people attending a match, or the takings from them

explanation.walkthrough: In British sport the attendance or money taken at a match is called by this word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a hinged barrier at an opening and the crowd figure or receipts at a sporting event.

clue.text: Bales out — a complete disaster

indicators.note: a disaster leaves things wrecked and jumbled, so the letters of the two words before are rearranged

explanation.surface: A farmer watches the bales tumble off the trailer, a complete disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disaster' turns BALESOUT into the answer; 'a' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: something complete or total is utter and unqualified.

clue.text: A dangerous job required a lot of money with order

parts.note: a bomb is British slang for a large sum, as in costing a bomb
disposal means arrangement or order, as in the disposal of troops

explanation.surface: A risky task demanded heavy funding and proper organisation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'required' and 'with' are link words. 'Cost a bomb' is British slang for being very expensive.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: the hazardous work of making explosive devices safe.

clue.text: Lover of Bess in musical heading off for wild party

indicators.note: the name's first letter, its head, is cut off

parts.note: Porgy loves Bess in Gershwin's opera Porgy and Bess

explanation.surface: A show's leading man drops out to join a riotous party.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: a wild and unrestrained revel or debauch.

clue.text: Philosopher passing through American customs

indicators.note: the philosopher goes inside the American abbreviation, as if travelling through it

parts.note: a sage is a wise thinker

explanation.surface: A thinker travels across the United States and passes through border control.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: habitual practices or conventions, the ways things are usually done.

clue.text: No more wine — that's the limit

parts.note: ex means former, no longer what it was
tent is a deep red Spanish wine

explanation.surface: A drinker finds the bottle empty and declares that's the final straw.
explanation.walkthrough: TENT is an old name for a dark red Spanish wine, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: the range or scope something reaches, its full reach.

clue.text: Bounds within which wines are stored

definitions.meaning: leaps or jumps, as a gymnast springs over a horse
underground cellars where wine is laid down

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both leaps over obstacles and arched cellars for keeping wine.

clue.text: He's bound to better himself elsewhere

definitions.text: He's bound to better himself elsewhere

parts.words: He's bound to better himself elsewhere
parts.note: bound reads as obliged, but means heading for: a man setting off to a new country to improve his lot

explanation.definitionFit: Someone who leaves their homeland to settle abroad, typically seeking a better life.

clue.text: Clearly they succeed in earning the dough

definitions.text: Clearly they succeed in earning the dough

parts.words: Clearly they succeed in earning the dough
parts.note: dough is slang for money, and the cd plays on bakers' loaves and on winning money for a household

explanation.walkthrough: 'dough' is slang for money, and the people bringing home a family's income split into bread plus winners.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: the earners whose wages support a household.

clue.text: For which there are bids in plenty

definitions.meaning: items put up at an auction
a great many, as in heaps or loads

explanation.definitionFit: Auction items are each called by this word, and informally it also means a large quantity.

clue.text: Booked with prejudice

parts.note: the word paired with prejudice in the title of Jane Austen's novel, so it is 'booked' alongside it

explanation.walkthrough: Jane Austen's novel 'Pride and Prejudice' puts the two words together in one book title.
explanation.definitionFit: Allusion: the companion noun in the title of Austen's famous novel about the Bennet family.

clue.text: Inadequate tip?

definitions.meaning: meagre or scanty, as in a thin harvest
to tilt or incline to one side

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an adjective for scant or meagre and a verb for tilting or inclining.

clue.text: A trial spin?

definitions.meaning: an attempt, as in give it a go

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an attempt at something and a rapid twirling movement.

clue.text: Soft cry of pain produces purse, but not of the lips

definitions.text: purse, but not of the lips

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, soft
ouch is what you say when hurt

explanation.surface: A gentle yelp of pain comes out of pursed lips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'produces' is a link word. 'but not of the lips' rules out purse as a verb, leaving the bag sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: a small bag or pocket for carrying money or tobacco.

clue.text: Hostile remark one was going to make

definitions.text: Hostile remark one was going to make

parts.words: Hostile remark one was going to make
parts.note: 'was going to' reads as intending, but means a parting jibe made while leaving

explanation.walkthrough: Parthian horse archers fired back at the enemy while riding away, so the phrase means a cutting remark made on departure.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a sharp parting comment, from ancient mounted archers who shot while retreating.

clue.text: Second mate at the wheel?

parts.note: reads as a ship's officer steering, but means a partner who shares the driving, as in rallying

explanation.walkthrough: 'Second mate' is a ship's officer rank, but here it means a partner who takes turns at the steering wheel of a car.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a rally partner or relief driver who shares the driving.

clue.text: Take part in a dramatic trial

definitions.text: Take part in a dramatic trial

parts.words: Take part in a dramatic trial
parts.note: reads as joining a sensational court case, but means practising a role before performing

explanation.walkthrough: 'Part' is an actor's role and the 'trial' a practice run, not a court case.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: practising a play or piece before the real performance.

clue.text: Terminated, so two cleared off

indicators.note: off suggests something gone wrong or out of order, so the letters of the three words before are rearranged

explanation.surface: A meeting ends once the last two people have cleared off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' turns SOTWOCLEARED into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: something that came to an end or was finished off has been concluded.

clue.text: Kept quiet in defeat

definitions.meaning: stayed out of sight, hid away
to bring down or overcome, as illness may do

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both hid away out of sight and knocked down or overcame.

clue.text: Find company in one churchman or another

indicators.note: the company abbreviation goes inside the churchman

parts.note: a dean is a senior clergyman

explanation.surface: Someone looks for a firm to join among the clergy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Find' is a link word; 'another' means another churchman, a cleric ranking below a priest.
explanation.definitionFit: Category: a junior cleric ranking below a priest, so a second churchman.

clue.text: Abraham Lincoln, to start with, was murdered

parts.note: Abe is the short form of Abraham, as in Abe Lincoln

indicators.note: takes the opening letter of the surname that follows

explanation.surface: A remark on the assassination of the American president Abraham Lincoln.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is an allusion: in Genesis, Adam's son was killed by his brother Cain, the first murder victim.
explanation.definitionFit: Allusion: the Biblical son of Adam slain by his brother Cain, so he is the one who was killed.

clue.text: Require sound massage

indicators.note: the word for require is to be heard spoken, giving its same-sounding twin

parts.note: to require something is to need it

explanation.surface: An aching patient insists they need a proper rub-down.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: to work and press muscles with the hands, as a baker works dough.

clue.text: The charge is about right, but you don't have to pay

indicators.note: the charge goes around the letter for right, encircling it

parts.note: a charge is a fee

explanation.surface: A shopper is told the price seems fair but that the item actually costs nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: an item you need not pay for costs nothing, being gratis.

clue.text: His eye's on the target

parts.note: reads as someone aiming carefully, but refers to the centre of a dartboard or target, named after a male bovine's eye

explanation.walkthrough: The centre of a target is called a bull's-eye, so the male animal's 'eye' is literally on it.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: the male bovine whose name gives the target's centre, the bull's-eye.

clue.text: It flows out of line

indicators.note: out of line means disordered, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something escapes from the queue and drifts away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' turns LINE into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the great African river, so a thing that flows.

clue.text: Reprimands for rules etc. Being broken

indicators.note: rules that are broken lose their order, so the letters of rules and etc. are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is scolded for breaking regulations and the like.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being broken' turns RULESETC into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: telling-offs or scoldings, as in being given a talking-to.

clue.text: Pirate's treasure?

parts.note: reads as a hoard of booty, but points to the pirate Long John in Stevenson's Treasure Island, whose name is also a precious metal

explanation.walkthrough: Long John is the pirate of Treasure Island, so the clue's 'treasure' is both his book and the precious metal his surname names.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname of Stevenson's one-legged pirate is also a precious metal found in treasure hoards.

clue.text: Turn a wench into a winch

parts.note: to turn a handle is to wind it
a lass is a girl, an old sense of wench

explanation.surface: A playful instruction to change one word into a near-rhyme by switching a letter.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface looks like a word ladder changing one vowel; 'into' is a link word joining the pieces to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: a drum turned by a crank to haul rope or chain, as on a ship.

clue.text: Qualification awarded in sixty minutes

definitions.meaning: an academic award such as a BA from a university
an angle unit made of sixty minutes of arc

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a university award and a unit of angle divided into sixty minutes of arc.
